newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo-Russian JV to boost Yugo business in Kuban.
newsitem.headline: Yugo-Russian JV to boost Yugo business in Kuban.

text.p: Seven Yugoslav companies joined a consortium of 10 Russian firms on Thursday and formed a joint venture aimed at boosting Yugoslav business presence in the southern Kuban region in Russia.
The new company, to operate under the name of Kuban-Yupred, will be located in the Black Sea town of Krasnodar.
The Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce representative in Moscow Djordje Jovic said the new joint venture will help Yugoslav companies get more contracts in the Kuban region.
"Kuban-Yupred will promote cooperation in construction, textile, leather, pharmaceuticals, food processing industries, and the banking sector," Jovic told reporters.
"One of the key aims is to establish cooperation in manufacturing industries and avoid taxes and customs duties through joint production," Jovic said.
Lola Korporacija, active in machine-building, and a construction giant Ratko Mitrovic Holding led the group of several smaller companies who joined Kuban-Yupred.
Vojvodjanska banka and Beobanka were seen coming to Krasnodar to help finance new projects, but neither bank showed up at the signing ceremony.
The founding capital of the new joint venture was estimated at around $20,000, with the Russian and Yugoslav side providing an equal stake.

"This is another step in Yugoslav-Russian cooperation, particularly in the field of construction industry. Yugoslavia has been and will remain a leading Russian partner in economic cooperation," Russian trade representative in Yugoslavia Lav Toshchenkov said, addressing a signing ceremony.

Russia was among Yugoslavia's largest trading partners in 1996. According to official statistics, 1996 exports to Russia stood at $156 million and imports at $225 million. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
